newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Kelley says US Q4 GDP likely be trend growth.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Kelley says US Q4 GDP likely be trend growth.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Edward Kelley said Tuesday that fourth quarter gross domestic product is likely to show trend growth.

"As far as I can see, we seem to be moving along without undue identifiable surges or air pockets, which would indicate to me that the most likely thing would be for another quarter of about trend growth," Kelley told reporters after speaking at a payments system risk conference.

Kelley also said that he did not see any "incipient surge" in inflation. "We are endeavouring to be very diligent in the face of what we all know is a very full, fully utilized economy, particularly in the area of employment," Kelley said.
"Very low unemployment rates are already causing wage pressures here and there, which could potentially be transferred over into price increases and inflation," Kelley said.
Kelley was asked about a report to be released Wednesday on the Consumer Price Index that is expected to show an upward bias of a percentage point or more a year in the index.

"We'll have to see what the evidence is that they cite, what the recommendations are that they may make and go from there. But it's much too preliminary now for me to try to say anything about that," Kelley said.
One area in the future that could boost the economy was consumer spending. Kelley said.

Real wages are starting to increase again and emerging wage pressures "could translate into consumer buying patterns, so if one were looking for where a surge could come from, that would seem to me to be the most likely candidate," Kelley said.
Another area that could be a potential source of economic strength was capital spending, Kelley said.
